A_target.statement:
Let $a_i, b_i$ be [[Definition:Integer|integers]] for $i = 1, 2, 3, 4$.
Then there exist integers $c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4$ such that:
:$\paren {a_1^2 + a_2^2 + a_3^2 + a_4^2} \paren {b_1^2 + b_2^2 + b_3^2 + b_4^2} = c_1^2 + c_2^2 + c_3^2 + c_4^2$

B_source.statement:
Let $p, q \in \Bbb H$ be [[Definition:Quaternion|quaternions]].
Then:
:$\map N {p q} = \map N p \map N q$
where $\map N q = q \bar q$ is the [[Definition:Norm of Quaternion|quaternion norm]].

substitutions.a sum of four squares a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2: the norm N(q) of a quaternion q = a + bi + cj + dk
substitutions.product of two such sums: norm of the product of two quaternions

derived.components of pq: the explicit bilinear expressions in the identity

object_map.reformulation: Encode each sum of four squares as a quaternion norm; the multiplicativity of the norm becomes the four-square identity when written out in coordinates.

validity_conditions: N(a+bi+cj+dk) = a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2, so sums of four squares are exactly quaternion norms.
The quaternion norm is multiplicative because quaternions form a composition algebra: N(pq)=N(p)N(q).
Expanding N(pq)=N(p)N(q) in components yields Euler's explicit four-square identity.
proof_plan:
Let $q = b_1 + b_2 i + b_3 j + b_4 k$ and form the product $p q = c_1 + c_2 i + c_3 j + c_4 k$.
The $c_i$ are integers, as the products of $i$, $j$, $k$ are $\pm 1, \pm i, \pm j, \pm k$.

By multiplicativity of the norm:
:$\map N {p q} = \map N p \map N q$
